name: DSP (Demonstrate-Search-Predict) - Composing retrieval and language models for knowledge-intensive NLP
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2212.14024 (v1 28 Dec 2022, v2 23 Jan 2023; cs.CL / cs.IR). Not peer-reviewed; this report is the precursor to the peer-reviewed DSPy paper (ICLR 2024).
authors_affiliation: Omar Khattab, Keshav Santhanam, Xiang Lisa Li, David Hall, Percy Liang, Christopher Potts, Matei Zaharia — all Stanford University. (Correspondence: Omar Khattab, okhattab@cs.stanford.edu.)
code_url: https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dsp (released with the paper; the framework was subsequently renamed/evolved into DSPy at https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy, ~34.9k stars, MIT license, actively maintained).
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy (the continuously-maintained successor framework; 100+ releases, 410+ contributors as of 2026). The original DSP repo redirects into this line of work.
task_domain: QA (knowledge-intensive NLP): open-domain question answering, multi-hop QA, and conversational QA. Framed as programmatic retrieval-augmented in-context learning (programmatic RAG) for knowledge-intensive tasks.
problem_setting: Offline, single-agent (single LM + single RM), in-context-learning setting with FROZEN models and NO fine-tuning of either the LM (GPT-3.5 / text-davinci-002) or the RM (ColBERTv2). The developer writes a Python program that orchestrates natural-language messages (and scores) passed between a frozen LM and a frozen RM through composable transformations grouped into three stages: DEMONSTRATE, SEARCH, PREDICT. Supervision is limited to a small k-shot set of end-task (question, answer) labels (e.g. 16 demonstrations for open/multi-hop QA, 4 conversations for conv-QA); intermediate transformations (hop queries, decompositions, query rewrites) are NOT labeled and are bootstrapped automatically via weak supervision in DEMONSTRATE. Inference is interactive within a single example in the sense that retrieval and generation are interleaved across multiple hops, but there is no environment/agent loop and no cross-episode memory. Evaluation uses subsampled validation sets (1000 questions / 400 conversations) averaged over five seeds.
what_is_retrieved: (1) Passages/documents from a knowledge corpus (Wikipedia), retrieved by the RM to ground predictions during SEARCH and to support demonstrations during DEMONSTRATE; and (2) demonstrations (training examples) selected from the small k-shot train set to be programmatically augmented (bootstrapped) into pipeline-aware in-context exemplars. The primary 'retrieval' grounding the answer is passages.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: a large pre-defined knowledge corpus (a Wikipedia dump, aligned per dataset — Dec 2016 / Nov 2017 abstracts / Dec 2018) indexed by ColBERTv2. It is not a growing/episodic agent memory; the index is fixed (though the paper notes the framework makes the search index a first-class construct that can be changed/updated over time). The small train set used for demonstration selection is also static.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed/scheduled top-k retrieval per query (e.g., k=2, 5, or 7 passages depending on program/stage), but the OVERALL objective across a multi-hop SEARCH is iterative completeness-oriented: the program decomposes a complex question and gathers supporting evidence over multiple hops (e.g., two hops for HotPotQA, fusing across n=10 generated queries per hop with CombSUM) rather than a single fixed top-k. Not a precision-driven variable-size recommendation; selection counts are developer-set per stage.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve, Reuse] primarily. Retrieve (yes — passages and demonstrations). Reuse (yes — bootstrapped demonstrations and retrieved passages injected into prompts). Revise (partial/no — DEMONSTRATE bootstraps and self-filters candidate annotations by correctness, a weak form of validation, but does not revise/adapt a stored case to a new problem in the CBR sense). Retain (no — bootstrapped demonstrations are cached per program run, not retained into a persistent growing case base).
explicit_cbr_grounding: False: DSP does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. It is positioned within retrieval-augmented in-context learning and 'programming' frozen LMs/RMs. (It does realize CBR-like Retrieve+Reuse mechanisms via demonstration selection/bootstrapping, but under different terminology.)
retrieval_unit: Two units: (a) text passage / document (the SEARCH unit — passages from a Wikipedia corpus retrieved by ColBERTv2, top-k per query); and (b) single demonstration / case (a (question, answer) training example, programmatically augmented with bootstrapped intermediate fields in DEMONSTRATE). The grounding retrieval unit is the passage.
index_source: Static corpus, offline-induced: a fixed Wikipedia passage index built with ColBERTv2 (late-interaction). No online/test-time growth of the corpus. (DSP notes retrieval is a first-class construct so the index could be swapped/updated, but in the experiments it is fixed per dataset.)
index_structure_topology: Flat passage index over a large corpus, retrieved via ColBERTv2 late-interaction (token-level MaxSim) search (efficient via PLAID). No graph/hierarchical/cluster topology over the corpus. (Multi-query result fusion uses CombSUM across retrieval lists, not a structured index.)
retriever_type: Dense neural retriever: ColBERTv2 (late interaction / contextualized token-level MaxSim over BERT), used off-the-shelf zero-shot. DSP is described as agnostic to the retriever, so essentially any RM can be substituted. The LM additionally acts as a query generator (generating hop queries / rewrites that are fed to the RM), making the combined SEARCH stage an LM-guided dense retrieval pipeline.
retriever_learning_signal: None for the retriever itself — the RM (ColBERTv2) is used FROZEN / off-the-shelf with no fine-tuning, and the LM is also frozen. There is no retriever training in DSP; the only 'learning' is in-context: DEMONSTRATE bootstraps demonstrations using end-task labels (weak supervision) — keeping intermediate annotations only when the zero-shot pipeline produces a correct answer — which programmatically shapes the prompts that condition the frozen LM's query generation, but this does not update retriever parameters.
query_construction: LM-generated, thought-conditioned queries: in SEARCH the LM is prompted (via templates) to generate hop queries and intermediate summaries, conversational query rewrites that resolve dialogue dependencies, and decompositions; multiple queries (e.g., n=10) can be generated and fused. For the simplest open-QA program, the raw question is used directly to retrieve k=7 passages. Demonstrations are selected via sample / knn / crossval primitives.
query_granularity: Both task-level and step/hop-level (two-level): a query is constructed per retrieval hop within SEARCH (step-level, conditioned on prior hops' summaries), and demonstration selection is done at the example/task level. Multi-hop programs re-query iteratively across hops.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative (multi-hop) for the multi-hop/conversational programs: SEARCH performs a fixed or bounded number of hops (e.g., 2 hops for HotPotQA, up to max_hops=3 with an 'N/A' termination condition in the v2 search transformation), retrieving anew each hop conditioned on accumulated summaries. For the simplest open-QA program, retrieval is one-shot (retrieve k=7 then predict). Retrieval is also invoked during DEMONSTRATE bootstrapping.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Programmatic / fixed-schedule with an LM-generated termination signal: retrieval is triggered by the explicit control flow of the DSP program (each hop in a loop), not by token-confidence or a learned router. In multihop_search_v2 the LM can emit a query of 'N/A' to terminate hopping (an agent-/LM-initiated stop condition); otherwise the schedule is a developer-fixed number of hops.
reranking: No dedicated learned reranking stage over retrieved passages. Instead DSP uses multi-query RESULT FUSION (a fused_retrieval primitive with a default CombSUM variant summing per-passage probabilities across retrieval lists from n generated queries). For PREDICTions, candidate answers can be re-scored/compared (self-consistency majority vote, RM-based 'rank' to find the most grounded prediction, or MCQ-style comparison), which is answer-level selection rather than passage reranking.
retrieved_context_refinement: Decompose-then-recompose and summarize: in multi-hop SEARCH the LM summarizes the context retrieved in earlier hops (a per-hop summary is carried forward together with the final-hop passages), effectively distilling/compressing intermediate evidence; multi-query fusion (CombSUM) recombines lists. DEMONSTRATE filters out examples where search/predict fails (distractor/failure filtering during bootstrapping). No cross-encoder reranking or explicit distractor-removal model.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tools/skills; retrieval is over text passages and demonstrations, not engineered tool/API descriptions).
index_content_separation: N/A / No: the corpus passages are both indexed (ColBERTv2) and loaded into the prompt; there is no lightweight-index-then-content progressive-disclosure split.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index or live protocol). The RM is invoked as a first-class construct via the 'retrieve' primitive; the paper notes the search index can be changed/updated over time, but there is no CRUD auto-sync, RapidAPI/REST/MCP/function-calling tool protocol.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no tools; DSP composes a single LM and a single RM over text passages, so there is no inter-tool dependency modeling).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: retrieved passages and bootstrapped demonstrations are inserted into LM prompt templates (Context / Question / Rationale / Answer fields) to generate grounded chain-of-thought rationales and answers. Demonstrations additionally serve as in-context exemplars that adapt the frozen LM to each transformation. Retrieval is woven into a multi-stage program (DEMONSTRATE -> SEARCH -> PREDICT) rather than a single retrieve-then-read step.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-plan-then-retrieve interleaved within an explicit program: the DSP program assigns control flow to code (not to the LM completions, contrasting self-ask), composing small transformations (generate query -> retrieve -> summarize -> next hop -> predict). SEARCH realizes incremental, multi-hop 'research path' planning where the LM proposes next-step queries and the RM gathers evidence; PREDICT can branch into n pipelines-of-transformations (PoT) and aggregate by majority vote. No MCTS/tree search; planning is programmatic/iterative.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-hop / per-transformation within a rollout: retrieval is interleaved at the granularity of each SEARCH hop (each hop = generate query + summarize + retrieve), and CoT reasoning is generated per PREDICT step; not per-token. Self-consistency operates per-answer across n=20 sampled chains; PoT branching samples n=5 full pipeline paths.
adaptation_mechanism: Bootstrapping with correctness self-filtering (weak supervision): DEMONSTRATE runs the zero-shot pipeline on train examples and RETAINS the intermediate annotations (generated queries, retrieved passages) only when the produced answer matches the gold label (e.g., EM/F1/precision thresholds), turning end-task labels into pipeline-aware demonstrations. Retrieved demonstrations are then reused largely verbatim as in-context exemplars; there is no per-test-case LLM-prompted case adaptation or RL reuse-finetuning.
retrieved_item_representation: Mixed surface forms injected as text: (a) raw retrieved passages plus LM-generated per-hop free-text summaries (distilled context), and (b) bootstrapped demonstrations rendered as structured prompt fields (question, generated hop queries, summaries, rationale, answer). All passed as natural-language text between LM and RM (no latent/soft tokens).
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Two levels: passages are raw evidence (with LM-distilled per-hop summaries adding a light abstraction layer), and demonstrations are single examples augmented with intermediate reasoning/query annotations (raw-to-lightly-structured exemplars). Not distilled strategies, reusable workflows, or procedural skills.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Decomposition + correctness-filtered bootstrapping + aggregation: breaking problems into small, individually reliable transformations reduces error propagation (explicitly contrasted with self-ask's 'self-distraction'); DEMONSTRATE discards demonstrations whose search or predict fails (filtering bad/distracting annotations); PREDICT uses self-consistency / majority vote over many sampled chains and RM-grounded answer selection to suppress unreliable single generations. No retriever-aware training (RM is frozen).
memory_type: none (no persistent cross-episode memory). The only stateful store is the static Wikipedia passage index plus a per-program-run cache of bootstrapped demonstrations; neither is an episodic/skill/workflow/graph memory that grows across tasks.
write_back: False (no test-time write-back to a persistent memory). DEMONSTRATE caches bootstrapped intermediate annotations for the current program/seed (the 'annotate' primitive caches successful intermediate predictions), but these are demonstrations for the run, not experiences retained into a growing store.
online_growth: No: the retrievable corpus index is frozen during evaluation and does not grow at test time. (The framework permits swapping/updating the index, but no online growth is implemented in the experiments.)
write_back_trigger: on-success only (within the bootstrapping/annotation step): 'annotate' caches an example's intermediate predictions only if the zero-shot pipeline answered it correctly (returns the example when pred matches answer, else None). This is offline demonstration construction, not deployment-time experiential write-back; there is no per-step or reflective write to a persistent memory.
failure_experience_usage: Success-only: failed bootstrap attempts (examples where search or predict does not produce a correct answer) are discarded (return None) rather than stored as negative/corrective experiences. No failure memory or success-vs-failure contrastive store is used.
memory_evolution_update: N/A / append-and-discard within a run: bootstrapped demonstrations are cached (append) when successful and dropped when not; stored entries are not mutated, merged, refined, or pruned over time, and there is no persistent evolving memory.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No: retrieval/demonstration selection is NOT a trained/RL policy. The RM is frozen off-the-shelf and selection is via fixed similarity (knn), random sampling, or cross-validation primitives, with multi-query fusion. The LM (frozen) generates queries via prompting, but no policy parameters are learned (no M-MDP/RL/value-based optimization).
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No: single LM + single RM, single program; no multi-agent or cross-framework memory/experience sharing. (DSP is a framework for composing one LM and one RM via programs.)
benchmarks: Open-SQuAD (open-domain version of SQuAD over Wikipedia 2016, processed per Khattab et al. 2021b), HotPotQA (open-domain 'fullwiki', 'hard' split, over Wikipedia 2017 abstracts), and QReCC (conversational open-domain QA over Wikipedia 2018). Validation-set results reported, subsampled to 1000 questions (or 400 conversations) across five seeds. Held-out tasks mentioned for future versions: Open-NaturalQuestions, FEVER claim verification.
benchmark_family: QA: open-domain QA (Open-SQuAD), multi-hop QA (HotPotQA), and conversational/multi-turn QA (QReCC). All in the QA / multi-hop family; not in web/embodied/tool/code/memory/decision-RL families.
baselines: Vanilla LM (few-shot in-context GPT-3.5, no retrieval; 16-shot for open/multi-hop QA, 4 conversations for conv-QA); Retrieve-then-Read (RM supports each example with retrieved passage(s) then LM reads — emulates SoTA open-domain QA pipelines); Self-ask (Press et al. 2022, contemporaneous; reconfigured to query the same ColBERTv2 index, evaluated with original prompt and with a Refined Prompt). Qualitative reference points (from related work, not apples-to-apples): No-retrieval LM SoTA (Si et al. 2022, code-davinci-002) and Retrieval-augmented LM SoTA (Si et al. 2022; ReAct / Yao et al. 2022 on HotPotQA).
key_metrics: Answer Exact Match (EM) and F1 for Open-SQuAD and HotPotQA; F1 and novel-F1 (nF1, Paranjape et al. 2022) for QReCC. Relative gains reported against vanilla LM, retrieve-then-read, and self-ask.
headline_result: On HotPotQA (open-domain, GPT-3.5 + ColBERTv2, 16-shot, no fine-tuning), the task-aware DSP program reaches 51.4% EM / 62.9 F1, vs Vanilla LM 28.3 EM, Retrieve-then-Read 36.9 EM, and Self-ask 25.2 EM — exceeding these baselines by 82% / 39% / 80% relative in EM respectively. Open-SQuAD: DSP 36.6 EM / 49.0 F1 (vs vanilla 16.2 EM, RtR 33.8 EM, self-ask 9.3 EM). QReCC: DSP 35.0 F1 / 25.3 nF1 (vs vanilla 29.8 F1 / 18.4 nF1, RtR 31.6 F1 / 22.2 nF1). Aggregate abstract claim: 37-120%, 8-39%, and 80-290% relative gains over vanilla LM, retrieve-then-read, and self-ask respectively across the three tasks.
ablations: Not a controlled component-ablation study; rather component-level design analyses and comparisons. (1) Open-SQuAD: DSP's self-consistency over many retrieved passages gives +8% EM / +6% F1 over retrieve-then-read, attributing gains to aggregating information across passages. (2) Reference comparison to fine-tuned systems: DPR 29.8 EM and FiD-base ~36% (5 passages) up to 48% (100 passages) on Open-SQuAD, suggesting DSP's PREDICT could gain further by aggregating more passages. (3) Self-ask 'self-distraction' failure analysis (it decomposes questions tangentially, e.g. answering 1997 vs 1858) motivates DSP's program-controlled control flow over LM-controlled flow. (4) Self-ask Refined Prompt vs original (e.g., HotPotQA 25.2->28.6 EM) shows prompt engineering helps self-ask but it still trails DSP. (5) Program design choices: multi-hop fusion across n=10 queries/hop, choosing summary by largest avg log-prob, fixed 2 hops for HotPotQA, k=5 passages split across hops; conv-QA fuses n=10 rewritten queries.
evaluation_decoupling: No: only end-to-end downstream task metrics (EM/F1/nF1) are reported. No separate intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / retrieval completeness) are reported.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome (final answer EM/F1/nF1). Process quality is examined only qualitatively (e.g., the self-ask 'self-distraction' error analysis and example decompositions), not scored with step-wise/process metrics.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Efficiency motivations stated qualitatively rather than with full $/latency numbers: uses FROZEN LM+RM (no fine-tuning, lower annotation/deployment overhead); ColBERTv2 chosen for efficient zero-shot search (via PLAID). Cost-control measures: subsample eval to 1000 questions over 5 seeds, each seed processing one-fifth of examples to limit LM API spend. Programs make multiple LM calls (e.g., generate n=20 chains for self-consistency, n=10 queries per hop, n=5 PoT branches) and multiple retrieval calls per hop — increased inference cost is traded for large accuracy gains. No explicit latency/token-count/dollar figures reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Developer-set, fixed selection counts per stage rather than an adaptive budget: open-QA uses 16 sampled demonstrations, annotate keeps k=3 bootstrapped demos, retrieves k=7 passages, generates n=20 CoT chains (self-consistency); multi-hop uses 2 hops with k=5 passages split across hops and n=10 fused queries per hop; conv-QA uses 4 conversations as demos, 5 retrieved passages, n=10 rewritten queries, n=20 predict candidates. Constrained by GPT-3.5's context window but k is mostly fixed by the program, not precision-driven.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing benchmarks rather than constructing a new one). Existing datasets used: Open-SQuAD, HotPotQA (open-domain 'fullwiki', 'hard' subset), QReCC; eval subsampled to 1000 questions / 400 conversations over 5 seeds.
builds_on: Retrieve-then-read / open-domain QA pipelines (Lee et al. 2019; Khattab et al. 2021b ColBERT-QA; Izacard & Grave 2020 FiD); ColBERT / ColBERTv2 late-interaction retrieval (Khattab & Zaharia 2020; Santhanam et al. 2022b) and PLAID (Santhanam et al. 2022a); GPT-3-style in-context learning (Brown et al. 2020) on GPT-3.5/text-davinci-002 (Ouyang et al. 2022); chain-of-thought (Wei et al. 2022; Kojima et al. 2022) and self-consistency (Wang et al. 2022c); bootstrapping/self-generated rationales (STaR, Zelikman et al. 2022; Auto-CoT, Zhang et al. 2022; Huang et al. 2022); multi-hop dense retrieval and condensed/iterative retrieval (Xiong et al. 2020; Khattab et al. 2021a Baleen; Qi et al. 2020 IRRR); query-rewriting/decomposition for conversational and multi-hop QA (Anantha et al. 2020; Geva et al. 2021); retrieval fusion / CombSUM (Fox & Shaw 1994); language model cascades (Dohan et al. 2022); RAG for knowledge-intensive NLP (Lewis et al. 2020); Hindsight (Paranjape et al. 2022).
contrasts_with: Self-ask (Press et al. 2022) — contemporaneous LM-controlled follow-up-question prompting that delegates control flow to the LM completions and suffers 'self-distraction'; DSP outperforms it by 80-290% and instead assigns control flow to an explicit program. Standard retrieve-then-read pipelines (Lazaridou et al. 2022; Izacard et al. 2022) — rigid single-shot retrieve-then-read that fails when simple search cannot directly answer. ReAct (Yao et al. 2022, reference comparison on HotPotQA, 35.1 EM). Fine-tuned weakly-supervised multi-hop systems (Baleen, IRRR) that require labeled intermediate hops/decompositions, whereas DSP bootstraps these from end-task labels only.
lineage: Group B (RAG task-solving / programmatic RAG pipelines). DSP is a foundational framework that generalizes 'retrieve-then-read' into composable multi-stage LM<->RM programs and is the direct conceptual+codebase predecessor of DSPy (Khattab et al., 'DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines', ICLR 2024), which adds automatic prompt/weight optimization (compilers). It sits in the lineage from RAG (Lewis et al. 2020) / retrieve-then-read toward agentic, programmatic, and self-improving retrieval-augmented LM pipelines, and is contemporaneous with self-ask and ReAct.
